verses.56:2: Tende piedade de mim, Deus, tende piedade de mim: * porque em vós confia a minha alma.
verses.56:2b: E {umbra} das vossas asas esperarei, * até que passe a iniquidade.
verses.56:4: {misit}, e me livrou: * {opprobrium} os que me {conculcantes}.
verses.56:4b: {misitdeus} a sua misericórdia e a sua verdade, * e arrancou a minha alma do meio {catulorum}: dormi perturbado.
verses.56:7: Prepararam um laço {pedibus}: * e {incurvaverunt} a minha alma.
verses.56:7b: Cavaram um fosso {faciem}: * e caíram nele.
verses.56:8: O meu coração está {paratum1}, Deus, o meu coração está {paratum2}: * cantarei, e {psalmum8}.
verses.56:9: {exsurge1}, minha glória, {exsurge2}, saltério e cítara: * eu me levantarei ao amanhecer.
verses.56:10: Eu vos darei graças entre os povos, Senhor: * e {psalmum10} entre as nações:
verses.56:11: Porque {magnificata} até os céus a vossa misericórdia, * e até as nuvens a vossa verdade.
verses.56:12: {exaltare12} {caelos12}, Deus: * e sobre toda a terra a vossa glória.

decisions.latin: Et in umbra alárum tuárum sperábo
decisions.why: *in umbra* is locative (where the hoping is done), not the object of *speráre* (so the D36 *esperar em* is not in play). *à sombra de* is how Portuguese says 'in the shade of'; 16:8b has *sub umbra* → *Sob a sombra*, a different preposition, so the two need not match. DRB 'in the shadow of thy wings', MS1932 *à sombra das tuas asas*.

options.label: na sombra
options.note: the preposition to the letter; less idiomatic.

options.label: sob a sombra
options.note: = 16:8b, but that is *sub*; the Latin varies.

decisions.why: The Altíssimus row: 7:18 = 12:6b moved the adjective before the noun so that the *verse* could close on an oxytone; 90:1 lets the proparoxytone stand at a mediant. Here it is a mediant, so the Latin's (and the natural) order stands, with the adjective lowercase (it qualifies *Deus*; it is not the name).

options.label: ao Deus altíssimo
options.note: Ruling; the Latin's order; MS1932 *ao Deus altíssimo*.

decisions.why: *benefácere* (εὐεργετήσαντα) 'to do good to'; the 48:19 row already says *fazer bem* (*quando lhe fizeres bem*); 114:7 *Dóminus benefécit tibi* should follow. The second colon repeats *Deum* as the Latin does. DRB 'who hath done good to me'. MS1932 *que tanto bem me tem feito* adds *tanto* and a perfect of duration.

options.label: me fez o bem
options.note: the article steers away from 'did me good' (as a medicine does).

decisions.latin: Misit de cælo, et liberávit me
decisions.why: *Misit* has no object in the Latin (ἐξαπέστειλεν, no object either); what was sent is named only in the next verse (*Misit Deus misericórdiam suam, et veritátem suam*). Kept objectless, as 55:7's bare *esconderão* after the Latinist; MS1932 supplies *(o seu auxílio)* in a parenthesis, which is his gloss. *liberáre → livrar* (row).

options.label: Enviou do céu
options.note: Ruling; as the Latin; 56:4b fills the object.

options.label: Enviou do céu o seu auxílio

forms.misit: Enviou do céu o seu auxílio

options.note: MS1932's gloss made text; supplies a noun.

decisions.why: ἔδωκεν εἰς ὄνειδος: 'gave over to reproach'. *oppróbrium → afronta* (open row; *opróbrio* failed two blind readers at 118:22). *entregar a* keeps *dare in* as a giving-over. DRB 'made them a reproach', MS1932 *cobriu de opróbrio* change the verb. 38:9 *oppróbrium … dedísti me* → *fizestes de mim a afronta* is another build (the person is the reproach there).

options.label: entregou ao opróbrio
options.note: the cognate; unknown to the Ps 118 blind readers.

decisions.why: D44: *conculcáre → calcar aos pés* (55:2–3, 90:13); the row named 56:4. The participle as a relative clause in the present.

options.label: pisam aos pés
options.note: Ps 7:6's local exception; crossed idiom per the Ps 55 stylist.

decisions.why: The Latin opens 56:4 and 56:4b with the same verb; keeping *Enviou* at the head of both keeps the anaphora (a repetition, rule 2) and the verb–subject order Portuguese allows. The colon is also a versicle (111-1, Pent01-1: *V. Misit Deus misericórdiam suam et veritátem suam: ánimam meam erípuit de médio catulórum leónum*, grep), and reads alone.

*cátulus → filhote* (open row, 16:12 *um filhote de leão*; this verse is named there). MS1932 *cachorros dos leões* is a dog in Brazil. Both Latin nouns are plural; *de leões* keeps the number, *de leão* is the generic Portuguese would also say. *erípere de → arrancar* (the row: a source is named).

decisions.latin: Fílii hóminum dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ
decisions.why: The Latin hangs *Fílii hóminum* as a topic and resumes it with *eórum* (DRB 'The sons of men, whose teeth are weapons'); not a vocative (*eórum*, not *vestri*). Kept as a topic with a comma and the copula Portuguese needs (D2). *fílii hóminum → os filhos dos homens* (row). MS1932 recasts as *têm dentes que são*. *arma → armas*, *sagíttæ → setas* (row).

forms.filii: Os filhos dos homens, os seus dentes são armas e setas
Os filhos dos homens têm dentes que são armas e setas

decisions.why: D44 (novácula row): *acútus* of an edge → *afiado*, of a point → *agudo*; a sword is an edge (51:4 *navalha afiada*). The copula supplied as in the first colon.

The refrain. Row *Exaltáre* (passive imperative, to God) → *exaltai-vos* (7:7a, 20:14; this verse named); the medio-passive as ὑψώθητι. Identical Latin, identical Portuguese in 56:6 and 56:12; Ps 107:6 will copy. Safe under rule 3 (past *exaltei*).

options.label: Sede exaltado
options.note: the passive to the letter (DRB 'Be thou exalted').

decisions.why: Two glossary rows disagree: *super (place) → sobre* names 56:6 and gives 8:2b *se elevou … sobre os céus* (*super cælos*, the same Greek ἐπὶ τοὺς οὐρανούς); the *Exaltáre* row pencils *acima dos céus*. *sobre* ruled: it matches 8:2b, the Paschal responsory that quotes it (*Super cælos, Deus*, Pasc5-4), and the second colon of 56:12 (*super omnem terram → sobre toda a terra*), so one Latin word stays one Portuguese word inside the verse.

options.label: acima dos céus
options.note: the *Exaltáre* row's pencilled form; MS1932 at 56:12.

decisions.latin: et in omnem terram glória tua (56:6) / et super omnem terram (56:12)
decisions.why: The refrain is not quite identical in the DO Latin: 56:6 has *in omnem terram*, 56:12 *super omnem terram* (checked in Psalm56.txt; the Greek has ἐπὶ both times; 107:6 has *super*). The Latin varies and Portuguese has the pair, so the variation is kept: *por toda a terra* (extent, 'into/over all the earth') against *sobre toda a terra*. MS1932 makes the same distinction (*por toda a terra* / *sobre toda a terra*). The second colon is left verbless in both, as the Latin (MS1932 supplies *brilhe*).

options.label: sobre toda a terra
options.note: = 56:12; the Greek's one preposition (D15's test would allow it).

options.label: em toda a terra
options.note: the preposition to the letter; loses the reach.

decisions.why: A dative of the thing aimed at. *aos meus pés* would be heard as 'at my feet' (a place); *para os meus pés* keeps the aim. *láqueus → laço*, *paráre → preparar* (rows). Natural order (D2).

options.label: aos meus pés
options.note: MS1932 *armaram laços aos meus pés*; heard as a place.

decisions.why: κατέκαμψαν; L&S *incurvo* 'to bend, bow'; trop. 'to bend, cast down'. The bending is the image and stays (rule 5). 68:24 *dorsum eórum semper incúrva* is the only other place (grep) and should match.

Row *ante fáciem → diante da face de* (open; the Hebraism kept). *fódere* with a pit → *cavar*, *fóvea → fosso* (rows; the *lacus / fóvea* row pencils this verse as *Cavaram um fosso diante de mim, e caíram nele*). Natural order, object before the adverbial.

options.label: diante da minha face
options.note: Ruling; the *fácies* row keeps the face.

options.label: diante de mim
options.note: the *lacus / fóvea* row's pencil; MS1932; drops the face.

decisions.latin: Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum
decisions.why: The *parátus* row (16:12 *pronto para a presa*) leaves this line to its psalm. **First copy of the doublet: 107:2 has the same first colon and will copy it.** Also the responsory of Epi2-3 and the Alleluia of Pent20-0 (grep). *pronto* is the plain word for 'ready' and keeps the line close to the Latin's length (14 syllables; *preparado* twice would add four). Cost: the Latin's echo 56:7 *paravérunt láqueum* / 56:8 *parátum cor* (Greek ἡτοίμασαν / ἑτοίμη too) — the snare they prepared, the heart that is prepared — is lost; *preparado* keeps it and is option 2. *firme* is the Hebrew's (נָכוֹן), DM1962's. Natural order with the copula (D2); the repetition kept whole.

options.label: preparado
options.note: MS1932; keeps the echo with 56:7 *prepararam*; heavier.

decisions.why: *psalmum dícere* renders ψαλῶ, so D25's *entoar* serves with the Latin's singular noun: 17:50 *e entoarei um salmo ao vosso nome*, and 26:6b *cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino* → *cantarei, e entoarei um salmo ao Senhor* — 56:8's colon word for word but for *Dómino*, so it is copied. 56:10 = the Paschal versicle (Pasc4-0, *V. Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine, et psalmum dicam tibi in géntibus*). **Doublet:** 107:2 and 107:4 have *psallam* there (D25 *entoarei salmos*), so Ps 107 will differ at these two words, as the Latin does.

options.label: direi um salmo
options.note: *dícere* to the letter; DRB 'rehearse a psalm'.

decisions.latin: Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara
decisions.why: **Doublet: 107:3 is identical and will copy this verse; the Epi2-3 responsory versicle is the whole verse.** The Latin says *exsúrge* (singular) twice, to the psalmist's glory and to harp-and-lyre; the repetition stays (rule 2). The addressees are not God, so *tu* (rule 3; the soul in 41:6 is *tu*); MS1932 *Levanta-te … levanta-te, saltério e citara*, the same singular. *exsúrgere → levantar-se* (row; *exsúrgam* → *eu me levantarei*, the subject named against the vocatives). *glória mea* (the self) is not explained (the row; MS1932's *minha alma* is his gloss); vocative without article, as *minha alma* in 41:6. *psaltérium → saltério*, *cíthara → cítara* (rows). *dilúculo → ao amanhecer* (row; 45:6, 118:148).

options.label: Levanta-te … levanta-te
options.note: Ruling; the Latin's singular twice; MS1932.

options.label: Levanta-te … levantai-vos
options.note: plural for two instruments; breaks the repetition.

options.label: Desperta … despertai
options.note: DM1962's verb (from the Hebrew עוּרָה); loses the *exsúrge / exsúrgam* echo with the row.

decisions.latin: Quóniam magnificáta est usque ad cælos misericórdia tua
decisions.why: ἐμεγαλύνθη, perfect passive. The pronominal form, as 8:2b *eleváta est … super cælos* → *se elevou … sobre os céus*; *magnificáre → engrandecer* (row). Latin order kept (verb, reach, subject), which Portuguese allows and which ends each colon on its noun. **Doublet:** 107:5 has another Latin (*Quia magna est super cælos*), so Ps 107 decides it locally; its second colon *et usque ad nubes véritas tua* is identical and will copy *e até as nuvens a vossa verdade*.

options.label: foi engrandecida
options.note: the passive to the letter; MS1932 *foi exaltada*.

choices.56:2: *Miserére mei* formula row, bare vocative *Deus*. *confídere in → confiar em* (24:1 *em vós confio*). The second colon is an antiphon on its own (*Quóniam * in te confídit ánima mea*, Monastic Lauds feria 3 and Wednesday Matins [Daya3]) and a short-responsory versicle (Matutinum Special [MM LB2C]); *porque em vós confia a minha alma* reads alone. The whole verse is a Mass chant (Quadp3-3, grep).
choices.56:2b: *speráre → esperar* (the future *esperarei*); *donec tránseat iníquitas → até que passe a iniquidade* (row).
choices.56:4: *e me livrou* — proclisis after *e*, the Brazilian order.
choices.56:4b: *dormívi conturbátus → dormi perturbado* (*dormíre → dormir*, 3:6; *conturbáre → perturbar*). *erípere de → arrancar* (row: the source is named). The Latin's comma after *misericórdiam suam* is not kept before *e*.
choices.56:6: The refrain. 56:6 and 56:12 share every slot the Latin shares (*Exaltai-vos sobre os céus, Deus*); they part at *in / super omnem terram* (see `interram`) and keep the Latin's own punctuation (comma / colon at the mediant).
choices.56:7b: *incidérunt in eam → e caíram nele*; MS1932 adds *eles mesmos*, not in the Latin.
choices.56:9: The mediant falls on *cítara*, a proparoxytone, as the Latin's *cíthara* does; kept (the Latin's word and order).
choices.56:10: *Confitébor tibi → Eu vos darei graças* (D5; 42:5 *Eu vos darei graças*); *in pópulis … in géntibus → entre os povos … entre as nações* (rows; 17:50). The trailing colon of the DO text kept. **Doublet:** 107:4 shares the first colon exactly and should copy it.
choices.56:11: *usque ad → até* (35:6 *até as nuvens*), Brazilian *até os* without *a*.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm56.txt, 14 prayed verses (56:2–56:12 with 56:2b, 56:4b, 56:7b); one mediant each, no flex. No titulus (D7). The refrain is not identical in the DO Latin: 56:6 *in omnem terram*, 56:12 *super omnem terram* (and comma / colon at the mediant). Liturgical uses (ps032/uses.py): 56:2 Mass chant Quadp3-3; 56:2a second half an antiphon (Monastic Lauds feria 3; Matins [Daya3]) and short-responsory versicle; 56:4b a versicle (111-1, Pent01-1); 56:8–9 the Epi2-3 responsory (R. *Parátum cor meum*, V. *Exsúrge, glória mea …*), 107:2's form in the Alleluia of Pent20-0; 56:10 a versicle (Pasc4-0). No use found for 56:6 = 56:12 as such.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps056.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rulings applied: D2, D5 (*darei graças*), D25 (*entoar um salmo* for *psalmum dícere*, as 17:50 and 26:6b), D36 (not met: *in umbra* is locative), D44 (*calcar aos pés*; *afiado* for an edge). Rows applied: Miserére mei, confídere, iníquitas, clamáre, Altíssimus, liberáre, oppróbrium (*afronta*), erípere (*arrancar* with a source), cátulus (*filhote*), conturbáre, fílii hóminum, sagítta, Exaltáre (*exaltai-vos*), super (place) (*sobre*), láqueus, paráre, parátus (*pronto*), fácies, fódere, lacus / fóvea (*fosso*), psaltérium, cíthara, exsúrgere, glória mea, dilúculo, pópuli / gentes, magnificáre. **Doublet with Ps 107 (glossary 'Doublets'): 56:8a = 107:2a, 56:9 = 107:3, 56:10a = 107:4a, 56:11b = 107:5b, 56:12 ≈ 107:6a are the first copy — Ps 107 will copy these wordings, so they were rendered to stand alone and to be copied; where Ps 107's Latin differs (*psallam in glória mea*, *psallam tibi in natiónibus*, *Quia magna est super cælos*) it decides locally.** Hard readings: 56:4 objectless *Misit*, *dedit in oppróbrium*; 56:5 the hanging *Fílii hóminum*; 56:6 vs 56:12 *in / super*; 56:8 *Parátum*; 56:9 the address.

Draft 1: hard pass (ids and marks). Soft length flags accepted: 56:2a +3 (*Tende piedade de mim* is the formula row, twice as the Latin); 56:4b −3 and 56:11a −3 (the Latin's long words); 56:4 second colon +3 (*calcar aos pés*, D44, is three words for one); 56:5b +3 (the copula and article supplied); 56:8a +5 and 56:8b +3 (the Latin's verbless *Parátum cor meum* twice needs *está* twice; the second colon copies 26:6b); 56:9b +5 (*exsúrgam dilúculo* is two words; *eu* named against the vocatives, *ao amanhecer* the row); 56:10b +3 (*entoar um salmo*, D25). Cadence: 56:9's mediant on *cítara* (proparoxytone) as the Latin's *cíthara*. No rhyme flags.
